**Target Users**: Working professional students + course instructors

## User Personas

### Sarah - Working Professional Student
- **Age**: 32
- **Role**: Product Manager at tech company
- **Context**: Pursuing graduate degree part-time while working full-time
- **Goals**:
  - Understand how to implement AI strategy in her organization
  - Balance coursework with demanding job
  - Get practical, applicable knowledge beyond theory
- **Pain Points**:
  - Limited time for synchronous learning (different time zone)
  - Needs quick clarification on complex concepts
  - Wants real-world business examples, not just academic theory
- **Needs from AI Tutor**:
  - 24/7 access to tutoring support
  - Bite-sized, focused learning modules
  - Practice with realistic business scenarios
  - Quick answers to specific questions

### Dr. Martinez - Course Instructor
- **Role**: Assistant Professor, AI Strategy
- **Context**: Teaching 100+ students in online program
- **Goals**:
  - Provide quality education at scale
  - Track student comprehension and progress
  - Reduce time on repetitive questions
- **Pain Points**:
  - Cannot scale 1-on-1 tutoring to all students
  - Difficult to identify struggling students early
  - Time-consuming to provide personalized feedback
- **Needs from AI Tutor**:
  - Analytics on student understanding gaps
  - Automated first-line support for common questions
  - Early alerts for students who need intervention
  - Ability to review/approve AI tutor responses

## Core Requirements

### Functional Requirements

#### P0 (Critical - Must Have for MVP)

**REQ-001: Interactive Q&A with Contextual Understanding**
- AI tutor answers student questions about AI strategy concepts
- Context-aware: understands course materials, student's progress, previous questions
- Provides relevant examples from business world (Google, Amazon, etc.)
- Suggests follow-up questions to deepen understanding
- **Acceptance**: Student receives contextually relevant answer within 3 seconds

**REQ-002: Personalized Learning Recommendations**
- System adapts to individual student's knowledge level
- Recommends next topics based on current mastery
- Adjusts difficulty based on performance
- **Acceptance**: System correctly identifies student level within first 3 interactions

**REQ-003: Case Study Analysis with Feedback**
- Present real-world AI strategy scenarios for analysis
- Student submits analysis, receives detailed feedback
- Feedback includes strengths, improvements, specific recommendations
- **Acceptance**: Feedback is actionable and improves student's next submission

**REQ-005: Explanation of Complex Concepts**
- Break down complex AI strategy frameworks (e.g., Porter's 5 Forces + AI, AI Transformation Playbook)
- Graduate-level explanations (not oversimplified)
- Include real-world applications
- **Acceptance**: 90%+ student comprehension on follow-up quiz

**REQ-008: 24/7 Availability Across Devices**
- Responsive web design (desktop, tablet, mobile)
- Always available (no downtime for student deadlines)
- **Acceptance**: 99.5% uptime, mobile scores 90+ on accessibility

#### P1 (High Priority - For Full Release)

**REQ-004: Concept Mastery Tracking**
- Track student mastery across all course topics
- Use Bloom's taxonomy for knowledge levels
- Regular concept checks

**REQ-006: LMS Integration**
- Integrate with Canvas (primary), Blackboard, Moodle
- LTI 1.3 standard for SSO and grade passback
- Deep linking for seamless experience

**REQ-007: Progress Tracking and Analytics**
- Student dashboard: see progress, time spent, areas for improvement
- Instructor dashboard: class-wide metrics, struggling students, common questions
- Exportable reports

### Non-Functional Requirements

**NFR-001: Performance**
- Response time < 3 seconds for 95% of queries (P95)
- P99 < 5 seconds
- Rationale: Students need quick feedback for engagement

**NFR-002: Scalability**
- Support 1000+ concurrent users
- Auto-scale during peak times (assignment deadlines)
- Rationale: Multiple courses, peak usage patterns

**NFR-003: Privacy & Compliance**
- FERPA compliance for student data
- GDPR compliance for international students
- Encryption at rest and in transit
- Rationale: Legal requirement for educational institutions

**NFR-004: Accuracy**
- 90%+ accuracy on concept explanations (validated by instructors)
- Low hallucination rate (grounded in course materials)
- Rationale: Educational quality must be maintained

**NFR-005: Availability**
- 99.5% uptime SLA
- Graceful degradation if components fail
- Rationale: Students may have assignment deadlines

### User Stories

**Story 1: Concept Clarification**
- **As a** student
- **I want** to ask questions about AI strategy concepts at any time
- **So that** I can clarify doubts immediately without waiting for office hours
- **Acceptance**: Question answered with relevant examples within 3 seconds, references course materials

**Story 2: Case Study Practice**
- **As a** student
- **I want** to practice analyzing real AI strategy cases
- **So that** I can apply theoretical knowledge to practical scenarios
- **Acceptance**: Case presented → student submits analysis → receives detailed, actionable feedback

**Story 3: Progress Visibility**
- **As a** student
- **I want** to see my progress on each course topic
- **So that** I can focus study time on areas where I'm weakest
- **Acceptance**: Dashboard shows mastery % for each major topic/framework

**Story 4: Class Insights**
- **As an** instructor
- **I want** to see which concepts students struggle with most
- **So that** I can adjust my teaching and provide targeted support
- **Acceptance**: Analytics show most-asked questions and lowest-scoring concepts

**Story 5: Quality Control**
- **As an** instructor
- **I want** to review and approve AI tutor responses
- **So that** I can ensure educational quality and accuracy
- **Acceptance**: Instructor dashboard for reviewing/editing tutor responses, feedback loop to improve

## System Architecture

### Architecture Pattern
**Microservices with Event-Driven Communication**
- Loosely coupled services for independent scaling
- Event bus for async communication
- Cloud-native on AWS

### Core Components

#### 1. API Gateway
- **Technology**: AWS API Gateway + Lambda
- **Purpose**: Single entry point, routing, auth, rate limiting
- **Scalability**: Serverless auto-scaling

#### 2. Tutor Service (Core AI Logic)
- **Technology**: Python FastAPI + LangChain
- **Purpose**:
  - Process student questions
  - Orchestrate AI reasoning chains
  - Generate personalized responses
  - Manage conversation context
- **Scalability**: Containerized (ECS) with auto-scaling

#### 3. LLM Integration Layer
- **Technology**: LangChain + OpenAI/Anthropic APIs
- **Purpose**:
  - Prompt engineering and management
  - API calls with retry logic and fallbacks
  - Response parsing and validation
  - Cost tracking and optimization
- **Patterns**: RAG (Retrieval Augmented Generation), Chain-of-Thought reasoning

#### 4. Knowledge Base Service
- **Technology**: Pinecone (Vector DB) + PostgreSQL
- **Purpose**:
  - Store course materials as embeddings
  - Semantic search for relevant content
  - Context retrieval for questions
  - Concept relationship mapping
- **Data Model**: Vector embeddings for semantic search, structured data for course outline

#### 5. Student Profile Service
- **Technology**: Node.js + PostgreSQL
- **Purpose**:
  - Manage student profiles
  - Track learning paths and progress
  - Concept mastery scoring
  - Interaction history
- **Compliance**: FERPA-compliant data handling, encryption at rest

#### 6. Analytics Service
- **Technology**: Python + TimescaleDB + Apache Superset
- **Purpose**:
  - Event tracking and aggregation
  - Student progress analytics
  - Instructor dashboards
  - Usage metrics and reporting

#### 7. LMS Integration Service
- **Technology**: Python + LTI 1.3 libraries
- **Purpose**:
  - LTI 1.3 authentication
  - Grade passback
  - User provisioning
  - Deep linking
- **Standards**: IMS LTI 1.3, LTI Advantage

#### 8. Frontend Application
- **Technology**: React + TypeScript + TailwindCSS
- **Purpose**:
  - Chat interface for Q&A
  - Progress dashboards
  - Case study interface
  - Instructor analytics
- **Deployment**: S3 + CloudFront CDN

#### 9. Cache Layer
- **Technology**: Redis (ElastiCache)
- **Purpose**:
  - FAQ response caching
  - Session management
  - Rate limiting
  - LLM response caching
- **Strategy**: Cache-aside pattern with TTL

### Data Flow: Student Question

```
1. Student submits question via Frontend
2. API Gateway authenticates and routes to Tutor Service
3. Tutor Service checks Redis cache for similar recent questions
4. If cache miss:
   a. Retrieve student context from Student Profile Service
   b. Query Knowledge Base Service for relevant course content (RAG)
   c. Construct prompt: context + question + relevant content
   d. LLM Integration Layer calls OpenAI/Claude API
   e. Parse and validate LLM response
5. Update Student Profile with interaction
6. Send event to Analytics Service (async)
7. Cache response in Redis
8. Return response to Frontend
```

### Key API Endpoints

**POST /api/v1/tutor/chat**
- Submit student question
- Request: `{question, context, topic}`
- Response: `{answer, sources, confidence, follow_up_questions}`

**POST /api/v1/tutor/case-study**
- Submit case study analysis for feedback
- Request: `{case_id, analysis}`
- Response: `{feedback, score, strengths, improvements}`

**GET /api/v1/analytics/student/{id}/progress**
- Get student progress
- Response: `{overall_progress, topics, engagement_metrics}`

**GET /api/v1/analytics/course/{id}/insights**
- Get instructor insights
- Response: `{class_performance, struggling_concepts, at_risk_students}`

### Technology Stack Summary

| Layer | Technology |
|-------|-----------|
| Frontend | React 18 + TypeScript + TailwindCSS |
| API Framework | FastAPI (Python) |
| AI/ML | LangChain + OpenAI GPT-4 + Claude 3.5 Sonnet |
| Vector DB | Pinecone |
| Relational DB | PostgreSQL 15 (RDS) |
| Cache | Redis 7 (ElastiCache) |
| Time-Series | TimescaleDB |
| Cloud | AWS (ECS Fargate, Lambda, S3, CloudFront) |
| Monitoring | Datadog + CloudWatch |

### Security & Compliance

**Authentication**:
- LMS users: LTI 1.3 OAuth 2.0
- Direct access: JWT with refresh tokens

**Authorization**:
- RBAC (student, instructor, admin)
- Enforced at API Gateway + service level

**Data Protection**:
- TLS 1.3 for all connections
- AES-256 encryption for PII
- FERPA: Student data isolation, audit logs, 7-year retention
- GDPR: Data export, right to deletion

**Accessibility**:
- WCAG 2.1 Level AA compliance

### Architectural Decision

**Decision**: Use RAG (Retrieval Augmented Generation) for Contextual Tutoring

**Rationale**:
- RAG grounds LLM responses in actual course materials
- Reduces hallucinations and improves accuracy
- Allows easy content updates without retraining
- Provides explainability (can cite sources)

**Alternatives Considered**:
- Fine-tuning LLM on course content → Rejected: high cost, difficult maintenance
- Rule-based system → Rejected: lacks flexibility
- Pure LLM without RAG → Rejected: accuracy concerns

**Implementation**:
- Pinecone for vector storage
- OpenAI embeddings (text-embedding-ada-002)
- LangChain for RAG orchestration

### Risk Assessment

| Risk | Severity | Mitigation |
|------|----------|-----------|
| LLM hallucinations | High | RAG pattern, confidence scoring, instructor review |
| API costs exceed budget | High | Aggressive caching, prompt optimization, usage monitoring |
| Student data breach | Critical | Encryption, security audits, FERPA compliance, minimal data collection |
| LMS integration failures | Medium | LTI 1.3 testing, fallback to direct login, detailed logging |
| Scalability issues | Medium | Load testing, auto-scaling, caching, graceful degradation |

## AI/LLM Strategy

### Reasoning Chains

#### 1. Concept Explanation Chain (RAG + Chain-of-Thought)
**Use Case**: Student asks about AI strategy concept

**Steps**:
1. Identify core concept from question
2. Retrieve relevant course materials (vector search)
3. Retrieve student's prior interactions (context)
4. Generate explanation using chain-of-thought
5. Include examples from course materials
6. Add follow-up questions

**Example**:
- Student: "What is AI-first strategy?"
- System: Retrieves course module → Checks student level → Generates explanation with Google/Amazon examples → Suggests follow-ups

#### 2. Case Study Analysis Chain (Multi-step Reasoning + Rubric Evaluation)
**Use Case**: Provide feedback on student case analysis

**Steps**:
1. Parse student's analysis
2. Retrieve case study details + rubric
3. Evaluate against rubric criteria
4. Identify strengths and improvements
5. Generate specific, actionable feedback
6. Provide score with justification

#### 3. Socratic Tutoring Chain (Iterative Questioning)
**Use Case**: Guide students to discover answers

**Steps**:
1. Identify knowledge gap
2. Generate probing question
3. Evaluate student response
4. Provide hint if stuck
5. Repeat until insight reached
6. Reinforce with summary

### Prompt Templates

#### Concept Explanation Template
```
You are an expert AI Strategy tutor for graduate students.

Question: {question}

Relevant Course Materials:
{retrieved_context}

Student Background:
- Completed modules: {completed_modules}
- Current level: {student_level}
- Previous questions: {related_questions}

Your task:
1. Explain concept clearly at graduate level
2. Connect to real-world business examples
3. Reference course materials
4. Check understanding with follow-ups

Requirements:
- Concise but thorough (200-300 words)
- Business examples (Google, Amazon, Microsoft)
- Avoid unexplained jargon
- Encourage critical thinking

Format:
[Explanation]
[Examples]
[Follow-up Questions]
```

#### Case Study Feedback Template
```
Evaluate this graduate student's AI strategy case analysis.

Case Study: {case_title}
Context: {case_context}

Student Analysis:
{student_analysis}

Rubric:
{rubric}

Provide:
**Strengths:** (specific examples from analysis)
**Areas for Improvement:** (why it matters)
**Recommendations:** (actionable next steps)
**Score: X/100**
**Justification:** (brief rationale)
```

### Model Selection Strategy

| Model | Use Cases | Rationale | Cost/Interaction |
|-------|-----------|-----------|------------------|
| **GPT-4 Turbo** (Primary) | Complex explanations, case feedback, Socratic tutoring | Best reasoning for nuanced education | $0.01-0.03 |
| **Claude 3.5 Sonnet** (Secondary) | Long context needs, detailed feedback | 200K context window | $0.003-0.015 |
| **GPT-3.5 Turbo** (Fallback) | Simple factual questions, FAQ | Cost optimization | $0.001-0.002 |

**Routing Logic**: Route based on question complexity + context length + budget

### Evaluation Framework

**Response Quality Metrics**:

1. **Accuracy**: 95%+ factually correct (instructor validation + fact checking)
2. **Relevance**: 90%+ directly addresses question (semantic similarity)
3. **Clarity**: Graduate level, Flesch-Kincaid 14-16, <20% follow-up rate
4. **Helpfulness**: 80%+ thumbs up from students

**Automated Checks**:
- Hallucination detection (verify claims against course materials)
- Citation validation (referenced sources exist)
- Completeness (all parts of question addressed)
- Safety screening (inappropriate content)

**Human Review**:
- 10% of responses reviewed by instructors
- Priority review: low-confidence, student-flagged
- Feedback loop: corrections improve prompts

### Safety & Guardrails

**Content Filtering**:
- Input: Filter inappropriate questions, prompt injections
- Output: Screen harmful advice, off-topic responses
- Tools: OpenAI Moderation API + custom filters

**Scope Limiting**:
- Only answer AI strategy related questions
- Don't complete assignments (guide thinking instead)
- Refer complex policy questions to instructor

**Confidence Thresholds**:
- High (>0.8): Provide answer
- Medium (0.5-0.8): Provide with caveat
- Low (<0.5): Acknowledge uncertainty, suggest instructor

**Prompt Injection Defense**:
- Input sanitization
- Clear system prompt boundaries
- Output validation
- Rate limiting on unusual patterns

### Personalization Strategy

**Adaptive Difficulty**:
- Levels: Novice, Intermediate, Advanced
- Determined by: Completed modules + quiz performance
- Adaptation: More examples for novice, more depth for advanced

**Learning Style**:
- Visual: Diagram descriptions, visual metaphors
- Example-driven: Heavy business case examples
- Theory-driven: Conceptual frameworks, research

**Pacing**:
- Fast-track: Advanced topics for quick masters
- Standard: Follow curriculum
- Remedial: Extra practice on struggling concepts

### Cost Optimization

- **Caching**: FAQ responses cached 24h
- **Prompt Optimization**: Minimize tokens, maintain quality
- **Model Routing**: Cheaper models for simple queries
- **Batch Processing**: Batch analytics queries
- **Monitoring**: Real-time cost tracking, budget alerts
